ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Conduct mandatory pre-incorporation and ongoing screening of all directors, officers, UBOs, and authorized payment-rail signatories against Global Affairs Canada's consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, and PEP databases reflecting domestic and foreign politically exposed persons together with prescribed family and close associates. Any PEP identification requires senior-management approval, enhanced due diligence, and verified source of funds and source of wealth. Screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry, operated by Service Alberta; official gateway at alberta.ca/corporate-registry, with name search filings submitted through authorized Alberta Registry Agents using the NUANS system.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Alberta Business Corporations Act and applicable name regulations, the corporate name must contain a distinct legal element indicating entity status; for an unlimited liability corporation the legal element 'Unlimited Liability Company' or the abbreviation 'ULC' is mandatory. Names must be rendered in Latin-alphabet script or translated/transliterated into English or French; non-Latin character names will not be accepted for NUANS clearance. The name must not be likely to cause confusion with an existing Alberta or Canadian corporate name, extra-provincial registration, or trademark. Bilingual English/French names are permitted.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation issued under the NUANS procedure is valid for 90 days and cannot be extended; if the reservation is not used within that period, a new name request and a fresh NUANS report must be filed. If the registry rejects a proposed name, the applicant receives a name-search report stating the grounds for refusal. The applicant may file a formal request for reconsideration with the Director of Corporate Registry within 30 days, attaching a fresh NUANS report, written consents from any affected trademark holder or regulated-body holder, and a statutory declaration explaining why the proposed name is not confusing. If the Director maintains the initial refusal, the applicant may seek judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Alberta Rules of Court. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately submit a corrected name reservation with a revised distinctive element and pay a new statutory fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Although an esports community platform operates entirely online, the Alberta Business Corporations Act requires every Alberta corporation to maintain a registered office in Alberta at a physical street address that is capable of accepting service of process during normal business hours. A mailbox-only virtual office does not satisfy the statutory registered-office obligation. A virtual office may be used as an administrative or head-office address, but the registered office must be maintained by a licensed Alberta registered agent or physical premises available for service.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, estimated 5–10% per annum for a fully online platform with no statutory physical-premises requirement. The likelihood rises to 30–50% upon a complaint, regulator inquiry, FINTRAC review, or discrepancy in corporate filings; Alberta Corporate Registry may verify registered-office availability and service capacity upon default or court order.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended, particularly Part 16.1, ss 268.1-268.6 governing Unlimited Liability Companies, together with the Business Corporations Regulation and the Corporate Registry fee schedule.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Ministry of Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction), Government of Alberta
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 02) filed electronically through the Alberta Corporate Registry online filing portal; accompanied by Form 27 (Notice of Registered Office and First Directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed under the ABCA for an unlimited liability corporation; shares may be issued without par value and for such consideration as the directors determine; no escrow account or paid-up capital deposit is required, and the corporation may commence business immediately upon issue of the certificate of incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the subscription agreements for the issuance of 100 Class A common shares at $0.01 per share be accepted, and the shares be allotted to the subscribers listed in the subscription schedule. RESOLVED FURTHER: that the registered office of the Company be established at the address shown in Form 27, Alberta, where the registered agent accepts service of process. RESOLVED FURTHER: that the following individuals be appointed as first officers: [Name] as President and Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Corporate Secretary, and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting. RESOLVED FURTHER: that the directors are authorized to open bank accounts, execute regulatory filings, and take all actions necessary to commence business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an approved NUANS search house or licensed corporate registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a licensed registry agent to run a NUANS name search on up to three proposed corporate names; the name must include a legal element identifying an unlimited liability corporation, such as 'ULC', 'Unlimited Liability Company', or 'Societe a responsabilite illimitee', per s 268.2 ABCA; upon receiving the NUANS certificate the name is reserved for 90 days.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report prepared within the last 30 days
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as confusingly similar, submit a revised NUANS report featuring a new distinctive element within the 90-day reservation window, or apply to the Assistant Registrar of Companies for discretionary approval with evidence of coexistence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation and Statutory Forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: In-house counsel, Alberta legal counsel, and the incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Form 02 expressly electing the unlimited liability regime under s 268.1 ABCA; ensure the corporate name contains the required ULC legal element; complete Form 27 naming the registered office and first directors; have each incorporator execute the articles and have signature verified by an Alberta lawyer or notary public.
required_dossiers: Form 27 - Notice of Registered Office and First Directors
Signed consent of each first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a regulatory defect is identified during legal review, amend and re-execute the forms before filing; no filing fee is incurred until submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Payment of Statutory Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) online filing portal through a registry agent direct access account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed Form 02 and Form 27 through the registry agent's secure portal; pay the CAD 200 filing fee by credit card or pre-funded registry deposit; the system issues an application number; the Assistant Registrar registers the articles and issues the electronic Certificate of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice, respond within 30 days with corrected documents; if the application is withdrawn before registration, request a partial refund of the filing fee as prescribed in the fee schedule.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Access Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Assistant Registrar of Companies, Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Retrieve the electronic certificate of incorporation from the portal; verify corporate name, ULC designation, registration number, and date of incorporation; obtain the corporate access number; print certified sealed copies for banking purposes; establish the corporate minute book and Common Records Register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For clerical errors in the certificate, apply under s 265 ABCA for rectification; for substantive changes, file articles of amendment (Form 03) with the prescribed fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and Adoption of First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors comprising the first directors named in Form 27
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting or execute a unanimous written resolution in lieu of a meeting; adopt By-law No. 1 adapted for ULC structure; adopt the pro-forma first board resolution covering share subscription, registered office adoption, and officer appointments; issue share certificates bearing a clear unlimited liability notice.
required_dossiers: Written resolution in lieu of a meeting
Minute book, register of directors, and register of allotments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a subscription default impairs allotment, allot shares to the remaining subscribers pro rata; if a director consent is found missing, file the consent late with the registry and pay the applicable late filing penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) through Business Registration Online; Alberta corporate tax administration coordinated with CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a nine-digit Business Number; activate the GST/HST account where taxable supplies are expected to exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold in four consecutive quarters; activate a payroll deductions account if employees are engaged; confirm the Alberta corporate income tax account is established; authorize representatives through the Represent a Client portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the application online through Business Registration Online within 30 days; late GST/HST registration may trigger a penalty equal to the greater of CAD 250 or 1% of net tax and may be mitigated through the CRA voluntary disclosure program.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Occupational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: City of Calgary or applicable Alberta municipal business licensing department; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS); Alberta Workers' Compensation Board (WCB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence for the office or commercial premises; for a purely digital esports matchmaking platform no provincial gaming or lottery permit is required because the platform is not a lottery under s 206 of the Criminal Code; if physical tournaments are held, obtain a special public event permit; register the employer with WCB and schedule an OHS office workplace clearance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal licence is refused for zoning reasons, apply for a minor variance or non-conforming use certificate; if WCB clearance is suspended, respond to the notice and file a corrective action plan to reinstate coverage.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the esports community platform is a digital software and matchmaking service (ISIC 5820 / NAICS 711219) with no industrial manufacturing footprint; no Alberta industrial licensing board has jurisdiction over the core service.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable at the provincial statutory level; a City of Calgary Business Licence Certificate may be required for office premises and a special event permit for any physical esports events.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the digital service operation falls outside Schedule A of the Environmental Assessment (Mandatory and Exempt Activities) Regulation, Alta Reg 55/2017; no registration or full EIA report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: General EPEA duty of care applies: no release of hazardous substances; zero industrial effluent; office waste and e-waste disposal per municipal by-laws and provincial electronics recycling programs; no wastewater, VOC, or air emission thresholds apply to server and IT operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification per the Alberta Fire Code (Alta Reg 194/2004) including annual inspection and certified extinguishers and exits; building structural load clearance issued by the municipality upon occupancy; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety clearance for the office under the OHS Act; Workers' Compensation Board coverage in place.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; business portal: CRA 'My Business Account' via canada.ca
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Canadian incorporated ULC, obtain the statutory Business Number (BN) by filing Form RC1 with CRA, either through the Business Registration Online (BRO) service or by mail. The ULC must also open a separate GST/HST program account and, as applicable, a corporate income tax account. A non-resident foreign entity not yet incorporated in Canada may register for a BN and HST account using the same Form RC1, supported by proof of Canadian nexus, a registered address for service, and corporate constitutional documents; a non-resident may be required to apply via the CRA international tax services office. The BN is the sole federal tax identifier for income tax, GST/HST, and customs obligations in Canada.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box regime for domestic tax purposes; a ULC is a separate taxpayer under the Income Tax Act. ULC hybrid status may be relevant for U.S. federal tax classification, for which Form 8832 may be used for U.S. purposes. Canadian statutory elections applicable to the enterprise include: (i) GST/HST election under subsection 156(1) for closely related corporations to treat taxable supplies as made for no consideration; (ii) joint GST/HST election for qualifying non-resident registrants; (iii) section 150(1) fiscal period election; and (iv) rollover elections under section 85 to transfer eligible property on a tax-deferred basis. Hybrid mismatch elections and agreement filings may be required under sections 18.4 to 18.6 of the Income Tax Act where a ULC is treated as a partnership or disregarded entity in a foreign jurisdiction.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); Alberta imposes only the federal 5% GST, with no provincial sales tax or HST surcharge
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies (worldwide) over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters, measured for small supplier determination; the same threshold applies to non-resident persons carrying on business in Canada
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No federal mandate for mandatory electronic invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance/API stamping for GST/HST. CRA accepts electronic records provided they contain the mandatory invoice data. A voluntary e-invoicing framework exists, and PEPPOL-aligned formats may be used for supply-chain efficiency, but CRA does not operate a digital stamping or clearance gateway. Quebec's provincial electronic invoicing rules (for Quebec QST) do not apply to an Alberta-based platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of tangible personal property qualifies for the 0% GST/HST export rate where the supplier sells the property and, as part of the supply agreement, ships or delivers it outside Canada to an address specified by the buyer, whether by common carrier, courier, or the supplier's own transport, and contemporaneous documentary evidence of export is kept. Services that are for the benefit of a non-resident person and performed wholly or primarily outside Canada may be zero-rated, provided the supply is not a supply of a service made to a person who is resident in Canada at the time the service is performed. Platform tournament access, matchmaking, spectator streaming, and prize-fund administration services supplied to non-resident esports organizations or overseas users will qualify for zero-rating if the 'place of supply' rules under section 142.2 are satisfied; subscription and fee-based platform services consumed within Canada are subject to 5% GST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (via Canada Border Services Agency, including secure export reporting under the Canadian Export Reporting System)
Bill of Lading / airway bill / outbound courier manifest showing the goods or equipment left Canada
Importer's purchase order or contract evidencing the destination of goods or services
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank ledger evidencing foreign currency receipt for the exported supply
Proof of payment received (wire transfer/payment gateway statement) matching the export sale
Complete GST/HST zero-rating evidence log including client name, non-resident status evidence, contract, and service-rendered records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may reassess a zero-rated supply and clawback the GST/HST benefit if the required export documentation is incomplete, if the non-resident status of the purchaser is not established, or if the goods/services are not in fact exported or supplied outside Canada within the relevant time. Penalties under subsection 285(1) of the Excise Tax Act apply to false or omissive statements; a knowingly false statement incurs a penalty of 25% of the amount of tax that would have been evaded, plus arrears interest. Criminal prosecution may expose officers, directors, and agents to fines and imprisonment for tax evasion. Additionally, the CRA may deny future zero-rating allowances and audit multiple fiscal years where a systemic export-zero-rating pattern is found, and a taxpayer may be held jointly and severally liable with its directors for unremitted GST/HST.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) in partnership with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for banking oversight, and the Department of Finance Canada for overall international financial policy. Currency transaction reporting is administered by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a comprehensively free and open currency regime under the Currency Act and the Bank of Canada Act. Both current account (trade in goods and services, royalties, and licensing fees) and capital account transactions (direct investment, portfolio flows, loans) are fully convertible into CAD and foreign currencies without exchange controls, quota restrictions, or discriminatory multiple-currency practices. Profit remittances, dividends, and branch repatriation amounts are freely transferable, subject only to general anti-money laundering (AML) reporting thresholds (e.g., FINTRAC reports for ≥ CAD 10,000) and to the corporate law solvency tests of the Canada Business Corporations Act or provincial equivalents. No prior administrative authorization is required for repatriation; only a ULC's unlimited liability feature and provincial tax filings may in practice lead to additional legal comfort letters for cross-border wiring.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not impose the surrender, conversion, or custodial requirement of export proceeds. Esports platform tournament fees, subscriptions, prize pools held in escrow, and sponsorship revenues may be settled in any invoiced currency. However, for accounting and tax harmonization, the functional currency of the Alberta ULC will be CAD; material non-CAD export receipts are marked-to-market under IFRS and section 95F of the Income Tax Act, and any realized FX gains are taxable as business income. No statutory timeline exists for repatriating export earnings into Canada.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (for investor funds) / Operational Account (daily tournament settlement)
Operational Account / Cross-Border USD Clearing Account
Operational Account / US Dollar Correspondent Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate feasibility with legal constraints. Canada does not issue European-style Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licences. A non-Canadian EMI may not obtain a passport directly; it must register as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC and hold a money transmitter licence in each province where it operates (most substantially via Alberta's Money Services Business Act registration). In practice, an Alberta ULC may use well-regulated offshore digital banking platforms (e.g., Wise Business, Payoneer, or an EU-licensed EMI) only as a settlement gateway for foreign currency receipts and contractor payouts, provided the EMI's flow is backed downstream by a Canadian Schedule I bank account. Legal constraints include FINTRAC-data residency, mandatory record keeping of large virtual currency transactions, and the prohibition of using an EMI as the sole treasury account because the ULC's statutory records and income-tax remittance accounts must be accessible to the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and provincial enforcement authorities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily required for an Alberta ULC. The bank will generally accept a remote opening application if the directors are known to the bank, or if the ULC provides an Alberta-registered law firm/accounting firm to attest the signatories' identities. In practice, each of the Big Six banks will require at least a video call interview with the beneficial owners and the designated signing officers (likely the Canadian-resident director, if any). For a ULC with non-resident directors, the onboarding manager may impose 'gestation period' Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) comprising (i) a physical meeting at the bank's downtown Calgary office for the ULC's president or a board-appointed attorney-in-fact, or (ii) a certified notarized identity attestation from a Canadian Consulate. Hence the practical mandate is soft physical presence: one key officer must appear in person or via video call with a notarized statutory declaration; full remote opening is permissible but only through a sponsor relationship with a Canadian law-firm trust ledgers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: ULC unlimited liability structure flagged as an opaque or hybrid pass-through entity, especially if the beneficial owner is a non-resident disregard entity for U.S. and Canadian tax purposes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Unanimous shareholder agreement and ULC articles certified by Alberta Corporate Registry; a legal opinion from a licensed Alberta counsel confirming the ULC is a separate legal person under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) and that unlimited liability applies to shareholders, not to the bank; CRA business number and GST/HST registration; specific comfort letter from a Canadian CPA confirming the ULC's tax classification as a disregarded entity or as a partnership for U.S. federal tax purposes (if applicable) and its Canadian income tax filing obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border tournament prize funds and 'prize pool custody' triggering suspicion of unlicensed gambling/money laundering due to high-volume microtransactions from an e-sports community.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform terms-of-service and game rules proving deterministic matchmaking and tournament outcomes, not wagering; Independent Regulatory Consultant's report (e.g., enhancing compliance) confirming no randomization of stakes or real-money betting; FINTRAC MSB registration certificate (if the ULC acts as a money transmitter for prize settlement); existing third-party payment processor (Stripe/PayPal) due-diligence packet showing no sanctioned transactions; audited statement of escrow accounting where prize pools are segregated into pooled trust accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Destination of platform subscription fees to foreign prize pools and contractor payouts in 'esports-protected jurisdictions' that are slow to respond to production orders (e.g., Malta, Cayman Islands, or a non-CAD payment rail).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed corporate domicile rationale for each counterparty; contracts with international payment processors to produce FATF-compliant transaction audit trails; anti-money-laundering (AML) policy and sanctions screening procedure aligned with Global Affairs Canada and United Nations regulations; proof of source of funds for any inward investment through lawyer-verified trust or corporate bank account statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultra-high-volume low-value revenue streams (microtransactions, in-game currencies) interpreted as potential layering activity through a dedicated corporate bank account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Operational dashboard and bank-integrated ERP reporting showing per-transaction metadata (gamer ID, match ID, tournament ID) matching statement line items; data-flow diagram from Stripe/PayPal settlement exports into the ULC accounting ledger; annual IT system control attestation (e.g., SOC 2 Type II report) for the platform's financial subledger.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For equity and shareholder loans into the Alberta ULC, international wire transfers must use the SWIFT MT103 message with a purposive narrative in SWIFT field 70. The recommended destination instruction is: [Beneficiary: CA_ULC entity name, city, province, country] with 'ACCOUNT TYPE: CAPITAL CALL' and purpose code 'S01' (Investment by direct resident investor) or 'S02' (Repatriation and divestment reversal) per Bank of Canada and OSFI guidance; where the sending bank requires ISO 20022, use the purpose code 'EQUI' for equity injection or 'LOAN' for intercompany debt. For debt injections, the ULC must execute a formal loan agreement with arm's-length interest rate in line with the CRA's prescribed interest rate and file Form T106 (reporting non-arm's-length transactions). Additional verification: inward capital wires are matched within five business days to the corporate registry's share allocation; stress-testing of exceptional non-straightforward relief from the Minister of Finance is unnecessary, but the bank may require a caveat on the wire's narrative to not trigger the Canadian Anti-Money Laundering verification of large cash transactions where the threshold of CAD 10,000 is exceeded in a single day.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The permissible clearing rails are: (i) SWIFT MT103 for ordinary operational disbursements (prize pool payments, contractor payments, gaming license fees) with beneficiary bank codes and narrative 'TRADE SETTLEMENT/ESPORT'; (ii) commercial letters of credit (L/C) via SWIFT MT700 for procurement of high-value hardware, broadcasting equipment, or infrastructure from foreign suppliers — typically available under an irrevocable, confirmed L/C from the ULC's Alberta or Ontario bank; (iii) bank drafts and automated clearing house (ACH) transfers for CAD/USD intra-Canada disbursements; and (iv) wire transfers through ClearPay or other wholesale systems for the settlement of in-game prize escrow accounts only where the destination account is a regulated financial institution. Outbound remittances over CAD 10,000 will trigger FINTRAC report (under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act) and an EDD check on the beneficiary; therefore the blueprint includes a dedicated 'prize settlement' correspondent account at a Canadian Schedule I bank managed in trust for the platform's winners.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Canadian-dollar versus euro outright forward contracts

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where the counterparty is a Canadian bank acting under the Canadian Foreign Exchange Market guidelines and the underlying payment is a CAD-inconvertible currency (not applicable to the primary CAD/USD and CAD/EUR exposures, but permissible as an overlay for exotic payments from regional esports markets)
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR) between the ULC and a Canadian chartered bank under an ISDA 2002 master agreement

Currency options (both purchased and written) executed within an ISDA and a Credit Support Annex (CSA), subject to the confirmation that the ULC does not fall under the 'speculative hedging' prohibition imposed by the Alberta Securities Commission for private issuers, and only using clearly identified underlying tournament revenue or procurement streams

Participating forwards and rolling forwards used to lock margin on annual sponsor revenue without creating an FX-linked derivative under the Canadian Derivatives Assessment and National Instrument 94-101

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Corporate Registry Information Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation under the Alberta Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of CAD 100 (approx. USD 75). Failure to file for two consecutive years permits administrative dissolution; the ULC must be reinstated before continuing business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal return including Alberta corporate income tax schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; tax balance is due earlier (two or three months after year-end depending on CCPC status)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month overdue, up to 12 months; repeat failures raise the penalty to 10% plus 2% per month, up to 24 months. Prescribed interest and director liability may also apply.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold is imposed by Alberta law. An independent audit is mandatory only if a reporting issuer, if the corporation is a distributing corporation under securities law, or if shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares demand an audit. Private non-offering ULCs may waive the auditor by unanimous shareholder resolution for each fiscal year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: CPA Canada Handbook – Part I (IFRS) for public/reporting issuers; Part II (ASPE) for private non-reporting enterprises, with voluntary IFRS adoption permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The ULC must maintain and annually confirm an Individual(s) with Significant Control (ISC) register. Share transfers must be recorded in the Register of Transfers, and ISC changes must be updated promptly as prescribed by the Alberta Business Corporations Act. The annual return confirmation requires the registered office address, current directors, shareholder and ISC data in good order before filing. An internal annual register audit should reconcile share certificates, transfer records, director consents and minute book entries to the filed annual return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individual(s) with Significant Control (ISC)
Minute Book (AGM minutes and written resolutions)
Register of Debentureholders (if debentures are issued)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200-500 per year for Alberta registered-office and corporate agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000-22,000 per year for a requisitioned independent audit; USD 3,000-7,500 for a review engagement when the audit is waived
